label: copy phase of short (L<=4) sequences
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (after the step that takes <DEL> as input; never on original tokens or the delimiter step) and mostly on short sequences: L=3 and L=4 hold about 87% of activation mass, with activation at about a third of all their steps, i.e. almost every copy step. The largest activations (near max) come at the first copy step (recall_idx 1, previous input <DEL>) of L=3 sequences, and they shrink on later copy steps. In longer sequences it fires weakly and patchily on the last 2-3 copy steps (to_go <= 2), favoring certain input tokens (x, m, h, i); this tail has about 13% of mass and no clean rule. Activation also drops when the original sequence contains many digits or repeated tokens. Predicate (phase 2 and L <= 4) gives dev precision 0.86, recall 0.65, F1 0.74, mass recall 0.87; misses are mostly weak long-L activations.
